---
title: "Where to Invest: Sensitivity Analysis"
subtitle: "Numerical sensitivity and inverse Roofline synthesis reveal where hardware budgets create value."
description: "Use partial derivatives of latency to identify the binding constraint for any model-hardware pair. Then invert the Roofline to derive minimum hardware specs from an SLA."
categories: ["analysis", "advanced"]
---

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
import mlsysim  # installed via `pip install mlsysim` (see workflow)
from mlsysim.solvers import ServingModel, SensitivitySolver, SynthesisSolver
from mlsysim.core.units import Q_

Engine = mlsysim.Engine

_model = mlsysim.Models.Language.Llama3_70B
_a100 = mlsysim.Hardware.Cloud.A100
_h100 = mlsysim.Hardware.Cloud.H100
_h200 = mlsysim.Hardware.Cloud.H200
_b200 = mlsysim.Hardware.Cloud.B200

_params_b = _model.parameters.to("Bparam").magnitude
_fp16_gb = _model.size_in_bytes("fp16").to("GB").magnitude
_int8_gb = _model.size_in_bytes("int8").to("GB").magnitude
_a100_cap_gib = _a100.memory.capacity.to("GiB").magnitude
_a100_cap_gb = _a100.memory.capacity.to("GB").magnitude
_a100_bw_tbs = _a100.memory.bandwidth.to("TB/s").magnitude
_a100_flops = _a100.compute.peak_flops.to("TFLOPs/s").magnitude
_a100_ridge = (_a100.compute.peak_flops / _a100.memory.bandwidth).to("flop/byte").magnitude

_sens_solver = SensitivitySolver()
_synth_solver = SynthesisSolver()

_res = _sens_solver.solve(model=_model, hardware=_a100, precision="int8")
_prof = Engine.solve(model=_model, hardware=_a100, precision="int8")
_res_fp16_a100 = _sens_solver.solve(model=_model, hardware=_a100, precision="fp16")
_res_fp16_h200 = _sens_solver.solve(model=_model, hardware=_h200, precision="fp16")
_res_fp16_b200 = _sens_solver.solve(model=_model, hardware=_b200, precision="fp16")

_sens_bw = _res.sensitivities["memory_bandwidth"]
_sens_flops = _res.sensitivities["peak_flops"]
_sens_cap = _res.sensitivities["memory_capacity"]
_elast_bw = _sens_bw / (_res.perturbation_pct / 100.0)
_elast_flops = _sens_flops / (_res.perturbation_pct / 100.0)
_mem_cmp_ratio = (_prof.latency_memory / _prof.latency_compute).to("dimensionless").magnitude
_ai_int8 = _prof.arithmetic_intensity.to("flop/byte").magnitude

_sla_ms = 50
_specs = _synth_solver.solve(model=_model, target_latency=Q_(f"{_sla_ms} ms"), precision="fp16")
_req_bw_tbs = _specs.required_bw.to("TB/s").magnitude
_req_flops = _specs.required_flops.to("TFLOPs/s").magnitude
_req_mem_gb = _specs.required_memory.to("GB").magnitude
_bw_vs_a100 = (_specs.required_bw / _a100.memory.bandwidth).to("dimensionless").magnitude

_gen_res = {
    "A100": _sens_solver.solve(model=_model, hardware=_a100, precision="int8"),
    "H100": _sens_solver.solve(model=_model, hardware=_h100, precision="int8"),
    "H200": _sens_solver.solve(model=_model, hardware=_h200, precision="int8"),
}
```

## The Question

A team has budget for one hardware upgrade. Should it buy more FLOP/s or more
memory bandwidth? Intuition suggests that more compute is always better, yet for single-stream `{python} _model.name` (`{python} f"{_params_b:.1f}B"` parameters) inference on an `{python} _a100.name`, a `{python} f"{_res.perturbation_pct:.0f}%"` bandwidth upgrade changes latency by **`{python} f"{_sens_bw:+.2%}"`** (an elasticity of $\frac{\Delta T / T}{\Delta \text{BW} / \text{BW}} = `{python} f"{_elast_bw:+.2f}"`$), whereas a `{python} f"{_res.perturbation_pct:.0f}%"` compute upgrade changes latency by **`{python} f"{_sens_flops:+.2%}"`** (memory transfer takes **`{python} f"{_mem_cmp_ratio:.0f}×"`** longer than compute). This tutorial computes those sensitivities
analytically and then inverts the Roofline to derive minimum hardware specifications from an SLA.

::: {.callout-note}
## Prerequisites
Complete [Tutorial 0: Hello, Roofline](00_hello_roofline.qmd) and
[Tutorial 1: The Memory Wall](01_memory_wall.qmd). This tutorial assumes familiarity with
memory-bound vs. compute-bound regimes and the ridge point concept.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Learning Objectives

- **Compute** numerical sensitivities of latency with respect to each hardware parameter
- **Identify** the binding constraint for any model-hardware pair
- **Quantify** the asymmetry between bandwidth and FLOP/s sensitivity
- **Derive** minimum hardware specs from a latency SLA using inverse Roofline synthesis
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Background: Sensitivity Analysis

In optimization, the **binding constraint** is the resource that actually limits
performance, the one holding with equality at the solution. `SensitivitySolver`
perturbs each hardware parameter (`peak_flops`, `memory_bandwidth`, `memory_capacity`) by a fixed percentage ($\Delta x / x = `{python} f"{_res.perturbation_pct:.0f}%"`$) and measures the normalized latency response
$\Delta T / T = (T_{\text{perturbed}} - T_{\text{base}}) / T_{\text{base}}$ (with corresponding elasticity $\frac{\Delta T / T}{\Delta x / x}$). The parameter with the
largest absolute response is the binding constraint and the lever most worth investing in.
:::

---

## 1. Setup

```python
import mlsysim
from mlsysim.solvers import ServingModel
from mlsysim.solvers import SensitivitySolver, SynthesisSolver
from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
```

---

## 2. Sensitivity Analysis: Llama-3 70B on A100

The analysis targets **`{python} _model.name`** (`{python} f"{_params_b:.1f}B"` parameters) inference on a single **`{python} _a100.name`** (`{python} f"{_a100_cap_gib:.0f} GiB"` / `{python} f"{_a100_cap_gb:.1f} GB"` HBM2e). At FP16 (`{python} f"{_fp16_gb:.1f} GB"` of weights), the model exceeds a single `{python} f"{_a100_cap_gib:.0f} GiB"` GPU and binds on `memory_capacity`; quantizing to INT8 (`{python} f"{_int8_gb:.1f} GB"` of weights) fits within HBM and exposes the steady-state hardware sensitivities.

```{python}
from mlsysim.solvers import ServingModel
from mlsysim.solvers import SensitivitySolver, SynthesisSolver
from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
from mlsysim.show import table, info

model = mlsysim.Models.Language.Llama3_70B
hardware = mlsysim.Hardware.Cloud.A100

# Compute normalized latency response to a 10% upgrade in each hardware parameter
solver = SensitivitySolver()
res = solver.solve(model=model, hardware=hardware, precision="int8")

info("Configuration",
     Model=model.name,
     Hardware=hardware.name,
     Baseline_latency=res.baseline_latency.to('ms'),
     Perturbation=f"{res.perturbation_pct}%")

rows = [[param, f"{sensitivity:+.4f}"] for param, sensitivity in res.sensitivities.items()]
table(["Parameter", "Sensitivity"], rows)
```

Each reported sensitivity is the fractional latency change $\Delta T / T$ for a `{python} f"{_res.perturbation_pct:.0f}%"` parameter increase. A sensitivity of **`{python} f"{_sens_bw:+.4f}"`** on `memory_bandwidth` (elasticity $\frac{\Delta T / T}{\Delta \text{BW} / \text{BW}} = `{python} f"{_elast_bw:+.2f}"`$) means a `{python} f"{_res.perturbation_pct:.0f}%"`
bandwidth increase yields an `{python} f"{abs(_sens_bw):.1%}"` latency reduction (from `{python} f"{_res.baseline_latency.to('ms').magnitude:.2f} ms"` to `{python} f"{_res.baseline_latency.to('ms').magnitude * (1 + _sens_bw):.2f} ms"`). A sensitivity of **`{python} f"{_sens_flops:+.4f}"`** on
`peak_flops` means additional compute produces zero latency reduction.

---

## 3. The Binding Constraint

```{python}
info("Binding Constraint",
     Constraint=res.binding_constraint,
     Interpretation=f"{res.binding_constraint} is the hardware knob most worth turning for {model.name} on {hardware.name}")
```

For `{python} _model.name` (`{python} f"{_params_b:.1f}B"` parameters) at batch size 1, every decode step streams `{python} f"{_int8_gb:.1f} GB"` of INT8 weights (plus activations) from HBM. The arithmetic intensity is `{python} f"{_ai_int8:.2f} FLOP/byte"`, far below the `{python} _a100.name` ridge point of `{python} f"{_a100_ridge:.1f} FLOP/byte"`. Memory transfer takes `{python} f"{_prof.latency_memory.to('ms').magnitude:.2f} ms"` while compute takes only `{python} f"{_prof.latency_compute.to('ms').magnitude:.2f} ms"`, confirming quantitatively that the workload is deeply memory-bound.

---

## 4. The Bandwidth vs. Compute Asymmetry

The asymmetry between memory bandwidth and compute throughput appears directly in the sensitivity comparison:

```{python}
sens_bw = abs(res.sensitivities.get("memory_bandwidth", 0))
sens_flops = abs(res.sensitivities.get("peak_flops", 0))

if sens_flops > 0:
    ratio = sens_bw / sens_flops
    info("Sensitivity Asymmetry",
         Bandwidth_sensitivity=f"{sens_bw:.4f}",
         FLOPS_sensitivity=f"{sens_flops:.4f}",
         Ratio=f"{ratio:.1f}x",
         Verdict=f"A dollar spent on bandwidth improvement is ~{ratio:.0f}x more impactful than the same dollar spent on more FLOP/s")
else:
    info("Sensitivity Asymmetry",
         Bandwidth_sensitivity=f"{sens_bw:.4f}",
         FLOPS_sensitivity=f"{sens_flops:.4f}",
         Verdict="FLOPS has zero sensitivity --- purely memory-bound")
```

::: {.callout-important}
## Key Insight

**Sensitivity analysis quantifies why bandwidth dominates single-stream LLM inference.** Under the Roofline model $T = \max(T_{\text{compute}}, T_{\text{memory}}) + T_{\text{overhead}}$, memory transfer for `{python} _model.name` on `{python} _a100.name` takes `{python} f"{_prof.latency_memory.to('ms').magnitude:.2f} ms"` versus `{python} f"{_prof.latency_compute.to('ms').magnitude:.2f} ms"` for compute (an **`{python} f"{_mem_cmp_ratio:.0f}×"`** gap). Consequently, a `{python} f"{_res.perturbation_pct:.0f}%"` bandwidth increase reduces latency by `{python} f"{abs(_sens_bw):.2%}"` ($\Delta T / T = `{python} f"{_sens_bw:+.4f}"`$, elasticity $`{python} f"{_elast_bw:+.2f}"`$), whereas a `{python} f"{_res.perturbation_pct:.0f}%"` compute increase yields `{python} f"{abs(_sens_flops):.2%}"` improvement ($\Delta T / T = `{python} f"{_sens_flops:+.4f}"`$). The binding constraint, not the headline spec, determines
where a hardware budget creates value.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## Fallacy: Investing in the Highest-Spec Number Maximizes Performance

GPU vendors advertise peak FLOP/s prominently (`{python} f"{_a100_flops:.0f} TFLOP/s"` on `{python} _a100.name`, `{python} f"{_h100.compute.peak_flops.to('TFLOPs/s').magnitude:.0f} TFLOP/s"` on `{python} _h100.name`) because the number is large.
For memory-bound workloads where $T_{\text{memory}}$ exceeds $T_{\text{compute}}$ by `{python} f"{_mem_cmp_ratio:.0f}×"`, a `{python} f"{_res.perturbation_pct:.0f}%"` bandwidth increase cuts latency by `{python} f"{abs(_sens_bw):.1%}"` while a `{python} f"{_res.perturbation_pct:.0f}%"` compute increase yields `{python} f"{abs(_sens_flops):.1%}"`. The datasheet headline and the binding constraint are often
different parameters, and sensitivity analysis shows which one actually matters.
:::

---

## 5. Inverse Roofline: From SLA to Hardware

Sensitivity analysis identifies which parameter is worth improving. The natural follow-up
is *how much* improvement a given performance target requires.

The `SynthesisSolver` inverts the Roofline model. Instead of "given hardware, what is
the latency?", it asks: **"given a latency SLA, what hardware do I need?"**

Suppose a deployment requires an FP16 inter-token latency (ITL) of `{python} _sla_ms` ms or less:

```{python}
synth = SynthesisSolver()
specs = synth.solve(
    model=model,
    target_latency=Q_("50 ms"),
    precision="fp16"
)

info("Inverse Roofline: Required Hardware",
     Target_SLA="50 ms ITL",
     Min_memory_BW=specs.required_bw.to('TB/s'),
     Min_compute=specs.required_flops.to('TFLOPs/s'),
     Min_memory=specs.required_memory.to('GB'))
```

Meeting a `{python} _sla_ms` ms FP16 SLA for `{python} _model.name` requires **`{python} f"{_req_bw_tbs:.2f} TB/s"`** of memory bandwidth (**`{python} f"{_bw_vs_a100:.2f}×"`** what `{python} _a100.name`'s `{python} f"{_a100_bw_tbs:.2f} TB/s"` provides), at least **`{python} f"{_req_flops:.2f} TFLOP/s"`** of effective compute, and **`{python} f"{_req_mem_gb:.1f} GB"`** of HBM capacity. This immediately explains why single-GPU FP16 exceeded the `{python} f"{_a100_cap_gib:.0f} GiB"` (`{python} f"{_a100_cap_gb:.1f} GB"`) `{python} _a100.name` and narrows the single-device search to high-capacity H100/H200/B200-class accelerators or multi-GPU tensor parallelism.

---

## 6. Generational Comparison: Whether the Binding Constraint Shifts

Sensitivity analysis also reveals whether **hardware upgrades shift
the binding constraint**. The comparison below spans three GPU generations for INT8 single-GPU inference:

```{python}
gpus = [
    ("A100", mlsysim.Hardware.Cloud.A100),
    ("H100", mlsysim.Hardware.Cloud.H100),
    ("H200", mlsysim.Hardware.Cloud.H200),
]

rows = []
for name, hw in gpus:
    r = solver.solve(model=model, hardware=hw, precision="int8")
    s_bw = r.sensitivities.get("memory_bandwidth", 0)
    s_fl = r.sensitivities.get("peak_flops", 0)
    lat = r.baseline_latency.to("ms").magnitude
    rows.append([name, f"{s_bw:+.4f}", f"{s_fl:+.4f}", r.binding_constraint, f"{lat:.2f}ms"])

table(["GPU", "BW Sens", "FLOPS Sens", "Binding", "Latency"], rows)
```

Across all three generations (`{python} _a100.name` at `{python} f"{_gen_res['A100'].baseline_latency.to('ms').magnitude:.2f} ms"`, `{python} _h100.name` at `{python} f"{_gen_res['H100'].baseline_latency.to('ms').magnitude:.2f} ms"`, and `{python} _h200.name` at `{python} f"{_gen_res['H200'].baseline_latency.to('ms').magnitude:.2f} ms"`), `memory_bandwidth` remains the binding constraint (`{python} f"{_gen_res['A100'].sensitivities['memory_bandwidth']:+.4f}"`, `{python} f"{_gen_res['H100'].sensitivities['memory_bandwidth']:+.4f}"`, and `{python} f"{_gen_res['H200'].sensitivities['memory_bandwidth']:+.4f}"`). In FP16 (`{python} f"{_fp16_gb:.1f} GB"` required), by contrast, `{python} _a100.name` and `{python} _h100.name` (`{python} f"{_a100_cap_gb:.1f} GB"` capacity) bind on `memory_capacity`, `{python} _h200.name` (`{python} f"{_h200.memory.capacity.to('GB').magnitude:.1f} GB"` capacity) exhibits a `memory_capacity` sensitivity of `{python} f"{_res_fp16_h200.sensitivities['memory_capacity']:+.4f}"` because a 10% capacity increase crosses the `{python} f"{_fp16_gb:.1f} GB"` fit threshold, and `{python} _b200.name` (`{python} f"{_b200.memory.capacity.to('GB').magnitude:.1f} GB"` capacity) shifts the binding constraint from `memory_capacity` to `memory_bandwidth` (`{python} f"{_res_fp16_b200.sensitivities['memory_bandwidth']:+.4f}"` at `{python} f"{_res_fp16_b200.baseline_latency.to('ms').magnitude:.2f} ms"`).
